questions.question: Describe I/O operator.
questions.solution_html:
• I/O operators in C++ are
  • << (insertion operator): used with cout to output data.
  • Example: cout << "Hello";
  • >> (extraction operator): used with cin to input data.
  • Example: cin >> x;
  • These operators are overloaded in the iostream library.
  • Constructor has same name as the class.
questions.final_answer: Constructor has same name as the class
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Estimate the advantage of using a structured programming language.
questions.solution_html:
• Estimate the advantage of using a structured programming language.
  • Easier to read, debug, and maintain.
  • Programs are modular (divided into functions).
  • Reduces code redundancy.
  • Promotes top-down design and logical program flow.
  • It is automatically called when an object is created.
questions.final_answer: It is automatically called when an object is created
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Interpret the meaning of polymorphism.
questions.solution_html:
• Interpret the meaning of polymorphism.
  • Polymorphism means “many forms”.
  • It allows the same function or operator to behave differently based on the context.
  • Types
  • Compile-time (function overloading, operator overloading)
  • Run-time (function overriding using virtual functions)
  • It has no return type (not even void).
questions.final_answer: It has no return type (not even void)
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Present the difference between Break and Continue in loops.
questions.solution_html:
• Present the difference between Break and Continue in loops.
  • Break
  • Terminates the entire loop immediately.
  • Used when an exit from the loop is required.
  • Example: exit on condition
  • Continue
  • Skips the current iteration and continues with the next.
  • Used to skip specific conditions inside loop.
  • Example: skip negative values
  • Used to initialize data members.
  • (Any two points fetch full marks.)
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Describe how can you recognize that a function belongs to a class.
questions.solution_html:
• A function that belongs to a class is called a member function.
  • It is declared inside the class definition.
  • Accessed using the dot (.) operator with an object.
  • Example: object.functionName();

questions.question: Examine how 2-D array can be represented in memory.
questions.solution_html:
• Examine how 2-D array can be represented in memory.
  • Stored in row-major order (row by row in continuous memory).
  • Example
  • int a = {{1,2,3},{4,5,6}};
  • Memory representation
  • a, a, a, a, a, a
  • Address formula
  • Address(a[i][j]) = Base + ((i * totalColumns) + j) * size_of_element

questions.question: Compare friend function and a member function.
questions.solution_html:
• Compare friend function and member function.
  • Friend Function
  • Declared using friend keyword.
  • Not a member of the class but can access private data.
  • Invoked like a normal function.
  • Member Function
  • Declared normally inside class.
  • Is a member and can access all members directly.
  • Invoked using object and dot operator.
questions.final_answer: Invoked using object and dot operator
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Differentiate between member function and non member function.
questions.solution_html:
• Member Function
  • Declared inside the class.
  • Accesses class data directly.
  • Called using object.
  • Non-Member Function
  • Declared outside the class.
  • Cannot access private data (unless friend).
  • Called independently.

questions.question: Define parameterised constructor
questions.solution_html:
• A parameterised constructor is a constructor that takes arguments to initialize object data
  • members.
  • Example
  • class Student {
  • int age;
  • public
  • Student(int a) { age = a; }
  • };
  • Allows different initial values for different objects.

questions.question: Why is virtual base class is used?
questions.solution_html:
• To avoid ambiguity in multiple inheritance (diamond problem). Ensures only one copy of
  • base class is inherited by all derived classes.
  • Example
  • class A{}; class B: virtual public A{}; class C: virtual public A{}; class D: public
  • B, public C{};
questions.final_answer: Option (b) virtual public A{}; class C: virtual public A{}; class D: public

questions.solution_html:

  • -Precedence/associativity of operators cannot change.
  • -Some operators like '.', '?:', 'sizeof' cannot be

questions.question: Analyze the effect of modifying a parameter in a function using call by / reference. What happens to the original variable?
questions.solution_html:
• Analyze effect of modifying parameter using call by reference.
  • Changes in function affect the original variable.
  • Example
  • void swap(int &a;,int &b;){int t=a;a=b;b=t;}
  • Original variables are changed.

questions.question: Explain hierarchical inheritance with suitable example and diagram.
questions.solution_html:
• Hierarchical Inheritance
  • When multiple derived classes inherit from one base class.
  • Example
  • class A{}; class B:public A{}; class C:public A{};
  • Diagram
  • Base Derived1, Derived2
questions.final_answer: Option (b) public A{}; class C:public A{};

questions.question: a) What is program structure of C++? b) Illustrate C++ Data Types.
questions.solution_html:
• a) Structure of C++ Program
  • Header files, namespace, class, function declarations, main().
  • Example
  • #include
  • using namespace std;
  • int main(){ cout<<"Hello"; return 0; }
  • b) C++ Data Types
  • -Basic: int, char, float, double
  • -Derived: array, pointer, reference, function
  • -User-defined: class, struct, union
  • enum

questions.question: Write two C++ programs to swap the values of two numbers: one using / call by value and the other using call by reference. Analyze the differences in the outputs and explain why the results differ between the two methods.
questions.solution_html:
• Swapping using call by value and call by
  • reference
  • Call by Value
  • void swap(int a, int b){ int t=a; a=b; b=t; } // No change in originals
  • Call by Reference
  • void swap(int &a;, int &b;){ int t=a; a=b; b=t; } // Changes
  • originals
  • Difference: Value uses copies; Reference uses actual
  • variables.
questions.final_answer: Option (b) { int t=a; a=b; b=t; } // No change in originals
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

  • Example
  • class A{public:int x;}; class B:public
  • A{}; Here, A is base class and B is
  • derived class.
